title: Lesson 3: Solving Quadratic Equations: Quadratic Formula
central_question: When a quadratic equation will not factor nicely, how do you still find where the curve hits zero — without guessing from a sketch alone?
intended_understanding: The quadratic formula is a reliable solve tool for ax^2 + bx + c = 0: students explore its algebraic development by connecting steps to a numeric example or following a demonstration (general-case reproduction is not required), then apply the formula using technology to find real roots. Standard form is the usual input; completing the square is assumed known from Lesson 2 and is not retaught. A light plant names when the formula beats factoring or graphing; the full strategy comparison waits for Lesson 4.
prerequisite_assumptions: Students can rewrite a quadratic from standard form to vertex form by completing the square, including simple rational b/a, and verify with graphing technology (Module 4 Lesson 2; A2.8). Completing the square is assumed known; this lesson does not reteach it.

Students can expand vertex form to standard form and verify with graphing technology (Module 4 Lesson 1; A2.7). This lesson may reuse that fluency softly when a model is not already in ax^2 + bx + c = 0; it does not new-teach expansion.

Students can determine real roots by factoring and by graphing, and can describe a connection between those two strategies (Module 3 Lessons 2–3; A1.8 M3 share). This lesson plants the formula as a third option when factoring is ugly; it does not reteach factoring or graphing.

Students can expand and simplify quadratic expressions, and can factor when a factoring strategy applies (Module 2; A1.2 and later factoring lessons). Those fluencies are assumed so that “will not factor nicely” is a recognizable situation, not a new skill.

Students already relate factors used in solving to x-intercepts of the corresponding graph (Module 3; A1.5). This lesson may reuse that roots-as-x-intercepts language softly; it does not new-teach the intercept connection or discriminant sign rules.
processes_to_teach: quadratic-formula-development-explore: Explore the algebraic development of the quadratic formula by connecting given steps to a numeric example or following a demonstration (with or without technology). Unassisted reproduction of the general-case development is not required. (A1.6 explore)
rearrange-to-standard-zero (optional): Rewrite an equation such as 100x^2 = 115x + 35 into ax^2 + bx + c = 0 so a, b, and c can be read for the formula.
quadratic-formula-apply-tech: Apply the quadratic formula using technology to solve quadratic equations for real roots.

classify-when-factor-vs-formula (light plant): Name when the formula beats factoring or graphing on a short ugly vs friendly pair — light plant only; the full advantages/disadvantages essay waits for Lesson 4.

purpose_map.purpose: Put students in a situation where they need the zeros (where the curve hits zero) but factoring is ugly or fails, so guessing from a sketch alone is unreliable. Completing the square is not practiced in the hook.

Have students try factoring and/or graphing on an ugly quadratic so they feel the limit of Module 3 strategies before the formula appears. Do not reteach factoring or graphing. (Analyze: which strategy is available.)
Rewrite an equation such as the Ministry example 100x^2 = 115x + 35 into ax^2 + bx + c = 0 so a, b, and c can be read. Cognitive target Apply. (rearrange-to-standard-zero)

Guided explore of the algebraic development — connect given steps to a numeric example or follow a demonstration (with or without technology). Students do not reproduce the general-case derivation unassisted. Cognitive target Understand. (quadratic-formula-development-explore)
Fully demonstrate applying the quadratic formula with technology to find real roots of a standard-zero equation. Cognitive target Apply. (quadratic-formula-apply-tech)

Repeat apply-with-technology on a second equation that varies signs or is not already in standard-zero form, so the first example is not a template to copy. Completing the square is not a required path. (Apply)

On a short friendly-vs-ugly pair, name when the formula beats factoring or graphing. Light plant only — not the full advantages/disadvantages essay (Lesson 4). Cognitive target Analyze. (classify-when-factor-vs-formula)
Return to the hook situation with a fresh equation that will not factor nicely: rearrange if needed, apply the formula with technology, and retrieve that general-case reproduction was not the goal.

hook_constraint: Need a situation where zeros matter but factoring is ugly or fails, so students cannot rely on a friendly factor or a guess from a sketch. Tiny context is allowed; this is not Lesson 5 modelling (A3.2 / A3.3). Do not practice completing the square in the hook. Prefer a lean Mobbin + Wonder visual if a hook visual is used. Consolidation must return to that same situation. No required login, Gizmos, or Desmos API. No Nelson formula stems.
instructional_sequence_intent: Need zeros when factoring is ugly (hook) → try factor/graph and feel the limit (minds-on) → rearrange to ax^2 + bx + c = 0 if needed → guided explore of formula development (no unassisted general-case reproduction) → worked apply-with-technology → varied apply-with-technology → light plant of when formula beats factoring/graphing → consolidation returns to hook with Key Idea / Need to Know.
